# Sushi benchmark data

`BTSBM` does not redistribute the Sushi Preference Dataset. Its licence
requires users to obtain the data from Toshihiro Kamishima and prohibits
redistribution without permission.

Use `sushi_toy()` for a reproducible synthetic teaching fixture. It has ten
sushi-type labels and known latent preference profiles, but contains no rows
from the original benchmark.

For research use, obtain the original dataset and review its licence at
<https://www.kamishima.net/soft/>. The benchmark is described in:

Kamishima, T. (2003). *Nantonac collaborative filtering: Recommendation based
on order responses*. Proceedings of the Ninth ACM SIGKDD International
Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining.
